text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees have agree to try and repatriate the last Vietnamese boatpeople from Hong Kong by the end of May.
-- Vietnam ranks among the world's top ten tea-producing countries, with 73,000 hectares of tea plantations yielding over 40,000 tonnes of tea a year.
-- National Assembly deputies, discussing a draft for amendments and supplements to the Criminal Law, called for more severe punishments to be imposed on corrupt officials and drug traffickers.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Secrestary Do Muoi told visiting Deputy Chairman of Cuba's State Council and Interior Minister Abelardo Colome Ibarra that Vietnam is determined to strengthen its solidarity, friendship and multi-faceted co-operation with Cuba.
-- Vietnam's first joint venture to produce equipment for optic cable conveyance, a $12-million project, has been licensed by the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
-- Vietnam and the United States reached a bilateral agreement on copyright protection.
